subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: After the prerequisite SQLite bootstrap lands, should OpenClaw accept this native-only PortGuardian migration exception and the one-way downgrade rule for macOS copies sharing the host-global state directory?
rationale: The PR deliberately changes durable host-global recovery state and relies on a signed mixed-version gate; automation cannot decide the supported downgrade and mixed-copy product contract.

options.title: Accept the bounded native cutover
options.body: Approve the native Darwin-lock and signed-copy exception after reviewing final-head proof and document that JSON-only downgrades cannot share the migrated state directory.

options.title: Require a different upgrade contract
options.body: Keep the PR open while maintainers specify a supported rollback or isolation path for older macOS app copies before accepting SQLite-only receipts.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded native cutover
recommendation.body: Approve the native Darwin-lock and signed-copy exception after reviewing final-head proof and document that JSON-only downgrades cannot share the migrated state directory.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored both the prerequisite native-state bootstrap and the PortGuardian migration series, and is best positioned to clarify the intended technical contract for maintainer approval.
